content:
MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
QA Automation Engineer | DevOps & Infrastructure
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Infrastructure-focused QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including recent hands-on work in CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes-based test environments, and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI pipelines supporting three product teams and has improved pipeline speed, reliability, and test-environment automation. Practical experience with Terraform, GitOps, monitoring, and TLS in personal infrastructure projects.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure and delivery: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes, k3s, Terraform, Argo CD, Ansible (basic)
Observability and networking: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Traefik, cert-manager, TLS
Programming and data: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, PostgreSQL
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Other: Linux, Git

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (approximately 25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages, and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into a dedicated stage; monthly CI runner costs fell by about 30%.
- Built short-lived merge-request environments using Docker Compose and later Helm on the shared Kubernetes cluster. Environments include the application, PostgreSQL and seeded data, and are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Enable QA and product teams to review features before merge, with end-to-end tests running against the environments.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; reduced the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Built Python tooling and Grafana dashboards using CI test results stored in PostgreSQL to identify flaky tests by team.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling to seed PostgreSQL test data.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Performed manual and automated testing of web and mobile applications for client projects.
- Introduced a Selenium and Java automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs for nightly regression runs.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS

Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Built a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform; used Ansible at a basic level.

Merge-Request Ephemeral Environments | Odrava Health | 2023–2024
- Implemented per-merge-request environments deployed via Helm to a shared Kubernetes cluster from GitLab CI, including an application, PostgreSQL and seeded data.
- Automated environment cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity, and enabled feature reviews and end-to-end testing before merge.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Helm, Kubernetes, Docker, Bash, PostgreSQL.

CI Pipeline Speed-up | Odrava Health | 2022
- Profiled pipelines for three teams, parallelised test jobs, added dependency caching and split end-to-end tests into a separate stage.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes and monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.
- Technologies: GitLab CI, Docker, pytest-xdist.

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional CV with a clear infrastructure and QA automation focus. The structure is easy to scan, achievements are quantified, and the selected infrastructure projects substantially strengthen the transition toward DevOps. The strongest evidence includes ownership of GitLab CI for three teams, the reduction in pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, ephemeral Kubernetes environments, and the reduction in flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The main limitation is not poor writing but incomplete evidence for several core requirements of this particular cloud infrastructure role. The document also presents the candidate as QA/infrastructure-focused rather than as an infrastructure engineer with demonstrated systems design, cloud operation, networking security, and stakeholder leadership experience.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: it uses conventional section headings, text-based formatting, standard dates, consistent job titles, and relevant keywords such as GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, Terraform, Docker, Prometheus, Grafana, TLS, Linux, Python, and PostgreSQL. The portfolio projects are particularly useful for keyword matching. AI screening probability is moderate to good for QA infrastructure, CI/CD, platform engineering, and Kubernetes roles, but lower for this specific vacancy because AWS, Terragrunt, mTLS, systems architecture, cloud infrastructure operation, and technical stakeholder leadership are not clearly evidenced. To improve matching without overstating experience, make the infrastructure-as-code, certificate-management, monitoring, and cross-team ownership language more explicit. Do not add unsupported terms such as AWS, Terragrunt, or mTLS.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a credible partial match. It demonstrates hands-on infrastructure engineering through Kubernetes-based ephemeral environments, Helm, Docker, GitLab CI, Terraform, monitoring, certificate management, and Linux. It also shows analytical problem-solving through pipeline profiling, test-result analysis, and measurable reliability improvements. Ownership of pipelines for three product teams and enabling QA/product review provide some evidence of leading technical topics and stakeholder collaboration. The strongest alignment with Corvale's values is end-to-end ownership, practical problem-solving, reliability, observability, and collaboration across product teams. Material gaps remain in strong Terraform and Terragrunt capability, AWS or comparable production cloud operation, mTLS, explicit systems architecture/system design, train/IoT/remote-device integration, and virtual-machine experience. The candidate also does not have documented backend or full-stack experience beyond Java test code. These are candidate-experience gaps, not defects that can be solved by rewriting the CV.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS
1. In the Professional Summary section, make the infrastructure transition and the scope of experience more precise by changing the opening to something like: "QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including the last two focused primarily on CI/CD pipelines, Kubernetes test environments, and build tooling. Owns GitLab CI delivery for three product teams and has hands-on experience with infrastructure-as-code, ephemeral environments, observability, and TLS certificate management." This uses supported evidence while improving alignment with infrastructure engineering and platform operation.
2. In the Technical Skills section, rename "Infrastructure and delivery" to "Infrastructure, IaC and delivery" and add the supported term "Infrastructure as Code (IaC)" before the existing tools. Keep Terraform, Helm, Kubernetes, Argo CD, and Ansible (basic) exactly qualified as shown. This improves ATS matching without implying unsupported Terragrunt experience.
3. In the Technical Skills section, change "Observability and networking" to "Observability, ingress and TLS" unless the candidate can substantiate broader networking work. Keep Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Traefik, cert-manager, and TLS. This accurately reflects the documented experience and avoids overstating networking or mTLS expertise.
4. In the Odrava Health experience section, revise the bullet beginning "Built short-lived merge-request environments" to make the operational scope clearer: "Built and operated short-lived merge-request environments using Docker Compose and later Helm on a shared Kubernetes cluster; provisioned the application, PostgreSQL, and seeded data, with automatic cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity." This better matches the ad's language around building and operating environments while remaining truthful.
5. In the Odrava Health experience section, combine the two environment-related bullets or revise the second one to explicitly show stakeholder impact: "Enabled QA and product teams to review features before merge and run end-to-end tests against isolated environments." This is clearer and more directly supports stakeholder collaboration.
6. In the Selected Infrastructure Projects section under "Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps," change "Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS" to "Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for observability, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS certificate management." The revised wording uses a relevant job term and accurately reflects the portfolio evidence.
7. In the Technical Skills section, add the supported keyword "GitLab API" under "Programming and data" or alongside Python. It appears in the original portfolio information for the flaky-test dashboard and can improve matching for automation and platform tooling roles.
8. In the Odrava Health experience section, revise the pipeline ownership bullet to emphasize cross-team technical ownership without claiming formal people leadership: "Own GitLab CI pipelines for three product teams (approximately 25 developers), coordinating build, unit, integration, end-to-end test, and artifact-publishing stages." This better supports the requirement for leading technical topics and bringing stakeholders along.

MINOR ATS / PRESENTATION ENHANCEMENT
9. In the document header, consider changing "QA Automation Engineer | DevOps & Infrastructure" to "QA Automation Engineer | CI/CD, Kubernetes & Infrastructure Automation". This is more specific to the documented evidence and may perform better for infrastructure-focused screening than the broad phrase "DevOps & Infrastructure."
